title: 1. Hook: The Invisible Building Blocks
text: Imagine tearing a piece of paper in half over and over again. Can you keep tearing it forever, or will you eventually reach a piece so small that it can't be cut anymore? Ancient philosophers wondered the exact same thing.

title: 2. Socratic Thinking
text: If everything around us—water, air, rocks, and even you—is made of particles so tiny we can't see them, how do you think scientists figured out what they look like on the inside?

content.title: 3. Discovery: The Atomic Models
content.description: Visualizing Dalton's solid sphere vs. Thomson's plum pudding.

title: 4. Reveal: Structure of the Atom
text: Atoms are not indivisible solid spheres. They contain subatomic particles: protons, neutrons, and electrons. The protons and neutrons are in the nucleus, while electrons orbit around it.

definition_preview: The smallest unit of ordinary matter that forms a chemical element.
A subatomic particle with a negative elementary electric charge.

question: Which of the following subatomic particles is negatively charged?

title: 6. Reflection
text: Think about it: If atoms are mostly empty space, why doesn't your hand pass right through the table? Try explaining it to a friend!

title: 7. Connection
text: In previous chapters, we learned about elements and compounds. The structure of the atom determines how different elements react with each other to form these compounds. This is the foundation of all chemistry!

title: 8. Mastery Challenge
description: Draw a model of a Carbon atom (Atomic number 6) showing the arrangement of protons, neutrons, and electrons.

title: Careful!
description: Don't confuse protons (positive) with photons (particles of light)!

title: Remember
description: The mass of an electron is negligible compared to a proton or neutron.
